description.p: Tug pulls every file over many connections and picks up exactly where it stopped, after a pause, a crash or a dropped connection. It is a download manager for Linux, made for KDE Plasma first. Its keyboard-first window shows what each download does, down to each connection.

ul.li: Each file downloads over up to 32 connections, and 8 by default. When a connection finishes its part, Tug splits the largest part that remains, so every connection stays busy to the end.
Tug saves its place as it goes, so a download resumes after a stop or a crash.
One queue takes web links over HTTP(S) and FTP(S), magnet links and .torrent files.
You set how many downloads run at once, a speed limit, a lower limit for busy hours, or a schedule.
When you add a download, you can give it its own folder, connections, speed limit, name, referrer, cookies and User-Agent.
The inspector shows a map of the file's parts, the speed of each connection, the server and the engine's log.
Tug shows a tray icon with a progress ring, notifications with Open and Show in folder, and its progress on the task manager.
